exposure: sociodemographic factors (maternal education level, household head sex)
cohort: The study included 340 mother-child pairs involving under-five children in Hawassa City, Sidama National Regional State, Ethiopia.
finding: Low dietary diversity, lower maternal educational level (secondary school or less), and belonging to a female-headed household were significantly associated with stunting among under-five children.
cross-section timing: Children under five years of age (0-5 years) at the time of data collection.
